site.name: larkfit-mobile
site.summary: larkfit-mobile Fictional fitness tracker "Lark" iOS-style mobile fixture. UXBench fixture in the Mobile Micro-UI category. Layout - 390 × 844 phone frame with chrome bezel, notch, status bar, home indicator - Bottom 4-tab bar: Today / Workouts / Activity / You - Edge-to-edge on actual mobile (≤460 px) Screens | `data-screen` | Highlights |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full larkfit-mobile system, prioritizing the primary docs/tutorial flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The “Today → workout detail → back to Today” flow works when the user taps the small play control on the Today plan (a workout detail page with PLAN/YOU’LL NEED and a “Start workout” CTA appears). However, key primary actions in the Workouts view feel unreliable or non-discoverable: the gear and the per-item “start” affordance are not evidenced, and multiple taps produce no visible change. Mobile usability is further weakened by consistently small touch targets and missing accessibility labeling on at least one dropdown.

exploration_plan.goal: Critique the full larkfit-mobile UX by exercising the primary Today → Workout entry path and validating adjacent bottom-tab flows (Workouts, Activity, You), including key states like starting a workout and recovering back to home.
exploration_plan.summary: Start on index.html and explore the primary Today plan interactions: the quick-launch play buttons and the “All workouts” entry. Then validate the adjacent bottom-tab destinations by switching tabs and checking whether content/state is preserved or reset. Throughout, pay attention to small-tap target issues flagged by the prescan and verify behavior on both desktop-sized and mobile-sized viewports (≤460px).
assumptions: The fixture is single-page (only index.html is present), with in-app navigation driven by buttons rather than separate HTML pages.
The bottom navigation buttons labeled ⌂ Today, ▶ Workouts, 📊 Activity, and ◉ You change views/sections within index.html.
The “Easy 5K — recovery” and “Hip-mobility flow” cards each have a play (▶) control intended to launch a workout-related flow/state.
The top-right “+” button likely adds/saves/checks something (e.g., quick action) and is worth validating even though it has a small tap target.
risk_hotspots: index.html: small tap target “+” (38x38) at ux-1; verify accuracy, accessibility, and touch friendliness on mobile viewport
index.html: small tap target “▶” controls for workout cards (36x36) at ux-2/ux-3; verify tap behavior (no mis-taps) and correct launch of intended workout
index.html: bottom tab buttons (⌂ Today / ▶ Workouts / 📊 Activity / ◉ You) at ux-4..ux-7; validate correct selected state, focus management, and return/navigation behavior
index.html: “All workouts →” / “All workouts” link-like CTA present in TODAY'S PLAN area; validate discoverability and whether it leads to the Workouts view/section

phases.title: Baseline capture + primary Today plan entry
phases.objective: Validate the default landing experience and the core Today plan interactions from the initial state shown in the prescan.
key_checks: Confirm visible header/date/user context and that the UI matches the prescan layout
Tap the “Easy 5K — recovery” play control (▶) and confirm the workout/session screen state changes as expected
Return from the workout/session back to Today (validate back affordance and whether the scroll position/selection is preserved)
Tap “Hip-mobility flow” play control (▶) and confirm it launches the correct second workout type/metadata
exit_criteria: Both workout play actions successfully transition to their respective workout-related states and can be exited back to the Today view
No console/network errors are triggered during these transitions

phases.title: Adjacent entry: All workouts + quick action (+)
phases.objective: Test alternative/adjacent navigation mechanisms that lead into the Workouts area and validate the top “+” quick action.
key_checks: Tap the “All workouts →” CTA in TODAY'S PLAN and verify it routes into the Workouts view/section (or expands a list) correctly
On mobile viewport, repeatedly tap the top-right “+” control (ux-1) to verify reliable activation despite the small tap target warning
If “+” opens an overlay/picker, validate that it can be dismissed (tap outside / close button) and that focus returns appropriately
exit_criteria: All workouts CTA leads to the intended destination and the user can return to Today cleanly
+ quick action is reliably tappable on mobile and its resulting UI (if any) is dismissible without getting stuck

phases.title: Bottom tab navigation consistency (Today/Workouts/Activity/You)
phases.objective: Validate the four-tab navigation model, including selected-state UI, content switching, and state persistence.
key_checks: Switch tabs in this order: Today → Workouts → Activity → You → back to Today; confirm active tab highlight/indicator is accurate
From Workouts, verify returning to Today shows either the same plan section or an intentional reset (record actual behavior)
Check whether workout launch state persists after switching tabs (e.g., if you start a workout then go to Activity/You, does it pause/exit?)
Verify there are no dead-ends: each tab must be reachable and must allow return
exit_criteria: All four bottom tabs switch correctly with consistent selected states
Navigation away from and back to Today is possible and behavior is coherent (no trapped overlay or broken transitions)

phases.title: Mobile-specific validation (≤460px) + tap target risk review
phases.objective: Re-run the most interaction-heavy checks on a mobile viewport and validate the prescan-flagged tap target risks.
key_checks: Repeat: tap “+”, tap both workout ▶ controls, and switch through all four bottom tabs
Specifically evaluate whether the 36x36–38x38 controls are still comfortable and do not trigger wrong targets
Check for layout shifts/clipping around the bottom tab bar and the workout cards when in the narrower viewport
exit_criteria: Critical interactions work as expected on mobile-sized viewport without mis-taps or clipped controls
Bottom tab bar remains visible and usable across transitions

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages (index.html only).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls per key page: + action, both workout play buttons, the All workouts CTA, and all bottom tab buttons (4).
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks from phases 1–3 on a mobile viewport (≤460px), with extra focus on the prescan small tap target warnings.

notes: Although the prescan reports only index.html, treat each distinct in-app view/section (Today/Workouts/Activity/You and workout session states) as separate exploration targets within the single page.

Keep step count efficient: prioritize transitions and back navigation over exhaustive clicking of non-primary metrics, since the fixture appears to be primarily a single-screen mobile UI with in-app state changes.

findings.user_goal: Start a selected workout from the Workouts list (e.g., Recovery) and receive clear confirmation/transition to an in-progress/session UI.
findings.problem: The UI suggests workout cards are selectable, but the expected transition/start feedback is not reliably triggered or not visually discoverable.
findings.evidence: On mobile, clicking workout-related targets (e.g., “All” and “Run”) changed the feed/filter state but did not produce a session/detail transition; the screenshot after taps still shows the Workouts list with cards and no workout-session view (“Workouts” list remains visible; no “Easy 5K · recovery” header or in-progress controls). Separately, the test attempting to click the workout control mapped to ux-20 timed out because the element resolved to a <select> and was not visible/enabled-stable (Click failed for ux-20: Locator.click: Timeout 4000ms exceeded).
findings.why_it_matters: If users cannot confidently start workouts from the list, the core fitness-tracking objective fails and trust in the app’s responsiveness drops.
findings.suggestion: Make the per-card action explicit with a prominent “Start workout”/“▶” CTA on each card (not just category chips), ensure it is visible/enabled in all states, and provide immediate UI feedback (loading state + session screen). If cards aren’t startable, clearly label them as “Browse”/“Details” and use consistent patterns to avoid ambiguity.
findings.source_hint: index.html (mobile screenshots in /_run/screenshots/agentic-79-click-mobile.png, agentic-80-click-mobile.png); Workouts list cards under header “Workouts”

findings.user_goal: Open Settings (gear) from the Workouts/You screen and get confirmation of the action (modal/drawer/navigation).
findings.problem: The gear icon is clickable but appears to be a silent no-op with no visible settings UI or dismissal/error feedback.
findings.evidence: On mobile, clicking ⚙ (target ux-11) resulted in no visible UI/state change: screenshot shows the same Workouts list and tool feedback reports changed=false. On desktop, clicking ⚙ (38×38px) also produced no observable change (tool_result: changed=false) and no dialog/overlay was evidenced.
findings.why_it_matters: Non-responsive controls break the interaction model and create uncertainty about whether the app is broken or whether the user tapped the wrong thing.
findings.suggestion: Ensure gear opens an accessible modal/drawer with clear title, close/dismiss affordance, and an explicit focus shift. If the fixture doesn’t implement settings, replace the gear with disabled state + tooltip (e.g., “Coming soon”) to avoid false affordances.

findings.user_goal: Use “All workouts →” / other Workouts entry affordances to navigate from Today to Workouts reliably.
findings.problem: The “All workouts →” control is inconsistent: in some cases it does nothing (no observable view change), while in other cases the user can reach Workouts via bottom tabs.
findings.evidence: Session notes indicate “Clicking the ‘▶’ control next to ‘All workouts →’ produced no observable change (URL/title unchanged), so the intended routing into a Workouts view was not confirmed.” In contrast, later evidence shows bottom tab switching works (clicking “▶ Workouts” changed the main header/content to “Workouts”).
findings.why_it_matters: Inconsistent routing from a prominent CTA increases cognitive load and makes users rely on secondary navigation (bottom tabs) rather than the designed entry point.
findings.suggestion: Make the “All workouts →” affordance behave identically to the Workouts tab: update header, selected tab state, and provide immediate visual feedback (e.g., highlight/transition). Add an in-place animation or loading indicator to confirm tap registration.
findings.source_hint: index.html (Today plan row containing “All workouts →” and its small ▶ control; earlier session signal about after_url unchanged)

findings.user_goal: Understand and operate time-range filters (e.g., Last 30 days / This week / This year) with assistive technologies.
findings.problem: The time-range <select> control lacks an accessible label (no label/aria-label/placeholder).
findings.evidence: Accessibility/layout warning: “Last 30 days This week This year” is a <select class="head-action" data-uxagent-id="ux-20">…</select> with no label, aria-label, or placeholder (console/layout warning: missing_input_label for target ux-20).
findings.why_it_matters: Users relying on screen readers may not know what the dropdown controls, harming task completion and trust.
findings.suggestion: Add a visible label and/or an aria-label describing the filter (e.g., “Activity time range”). Ensure the selected value is announced and focus behavior is correct after selection.
findings.source_hint: index.html → Activity screen top dropdown (target ux-20)

findings.user_goal: Tap primary controls (Start, back, gear, chips) accurately on mobile.
findings.problem: Multiple key tap targets are below mobile tap-size guidance, increasing mis-taps and the perception of broken UI.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag small tap targets: ⚙ is 38×38px (<44px guidance), “All” 46×30px, “Run” 55×30px, and the bottom back arrow “←” is 36×36px. The app also uses small play/arrow icons (e.g., ▶ 36×36px) that are repeatedly involved in no-op/timed-out interactions.
findings.why_it_matters: On small screens, undersized targets cause accidental misses and require repeated taps—especially problematic when controls already appear inconsistent.
findings.suggestion: Increase tap target size to at least 44×44px (or apply generous padding around icons), add spacing between adjacent controls, and ensure visual hit areas align with visible UI.
findings.source_hint: index.html → Workouts and workout-detail views (layout_warning_count=8; specific targets ux-11, ux-13/ux-14, ux-8, ux-3/ux-9)
